newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bankrupt Gdansk shipyard to host disco.
newsitem.headline: Polish bankrupt Gdansk shipyard to host disco.

text.p: Poland's bankrupt Gdansk shipyard, birthplace of the Solidarity movement that toppled communism in 1989, will host a disco club on its site to earn money it could not attract by building ships.

The shipyard, which fell victim to free market reforms it helped to initiate, has rented one of its six empty production halls to a company which is developing a night club there, said Piotr Grezicki, an aide of the yard's administrator.
"Rent for the 2000 square-metres hall is being paid regularly and this money is useful when there is no financial liquidity," Grezicki told Reuters.
The plan drew criticism from Lech Walesa -- Poland's previous president, who helped found Solidarity as an electrician in the shipyard 17 years ago.
"It sounds like a bad joke," he said.

The government is trying to find an investor to buy assets of the yard, which went bankrupt last year with debts exceeding 415 million zlotys ($134 million). The yard was forced to dismiss almost all of its 7,000-strong workforce.
